question.problem: Given that ![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14168227/assets/d61f758057cada0aebaa7d21c736121295f3f65f4621d065fa0c7ae1ca040af4.svg) express the quadratic form $Q(\mathbf{x})= x_1^2-x_2^2\,$ in terms of the components of $\mathbf{y}.$
question.worked_solution:
First, notice that  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14168227/assets/97f99e2e86ecbd0d4b913c2e3a6df61f90092df8aaa31d094b80d3d69a17727c.svg)

gives the following expressions for $x_1$ and $x_2\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}_{1} & ={y}_{1}-{y}_{2} \\ {x}_{2} & =2{y}_{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we substitute these into our quadratic form expression:

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & ={x}_{1}^{2}-{x}_{2}^{2} \\  & =({y}_{1}-{y}_{2})^{2}-(2{y}_{2})^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{1}{y}_{2}+{y}_{2}^{2}-4{y}_{2}^{2} \\  & ={y}_{1}^{2}-2{y}_{1}{y}_{2}-3{y}_{2}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$
